program: Reads a CSV file of money entries (date, account, amount in cents, memo) and prints totals by account and by month, the smallest entry, and the grand total. Amounts stay whole cents, so no rounding creeps in. Run it with a file: ters run examples/ledger examples/ledger/book.csv. A bad line stops it with the line's number.
1o9trcpga0se9ndcngel7b0aq2: Given one file name, runs the ledger on it; a problem anywhere (a bad line, an empty file) comes back as an abort and is printed by failed. Anything else on the command line prints how to use it. The Int is the exit code: 0 done, 1 failed, 2 used wrongly.
fg8h8467a8smuif1326u38jpjo: One line of the file: when, which account, how many cents (negative for money spent) and a note.
e3olsn5f7mqc2aoq8mrcl3a4en: A sum kept for one name (an account or a month): the cents added up and how many entries went in.
ib2770132r9jetcvqc22oqnhum: An empty line, or a comment starting with #, which the file may have and the ledger skips.
06ck4scdetvs0s8jmv94cr3io9: The cents field read as a whole number, or a stop that names line n.
rmpone71pfpefp315qmtiosoo8: The stop for a line that doesn't split into four fields.
u80s41pi72id0d1ab93d6up3ic: One line into an Entry: split at the commas, which must give exactly four fields.
gbfjtrhqvah1c12mhu9g62raii: Every line of the file as an Entry, counting lines from n so a stop can say which one; blank lines are skipped but still counted.
h8vmdutmm4ec790ptidd3er9bs: Adds cents to the total with this name, or starts one at the end if there is none yet.
84t03araust4i1katt7af1mt4i: The year and month of an entry, the first seven characters of its date (2026-07).
o51c8b6k1d8fnftt7j875p5a3k: Puts one total into an already sorted list in its place, by name or by size.
v6ksd74983l1p2c1pp9joctnij: Whether a has more cents than b; equal sums go by name, so the order is always the same.
3l6tpnn0jealbfk64p58k73n5c: The order the tables use: by name for months (oldest first), by size for accounts.
6babh9qtl5pq32ojjbc9m3k2ii: Insertion sort of the totals, one insert at a time.
r3bui40r7k0n3me7fngo0pqn98: The text with 0s in front until it is width long: 5 cents is 005, so it can be written 0.05.
p279bni5a2fk5ri3i3pb419ffj: The text with spaces in front until it is width long, for right-aligned columns.
3mr507liic1d7h9eihqvd6b7pn: The text with spaces after it until it is width long, for left-aligned columns.
6h2ulisjvqlig6hba43837h1ec: Puts a decimal point before the last two digits: 12345 becomes 123.45.
cfocanmdf9fp80lddvmd4ggo1h: Cents written as an amount with a point and a sign: -9042 is -90.42.
okh7juimrmi73k9ljv7gt8ltfu: One line of a table: the name, the sum lined up on the right, and how many entries.
0tqqt0bjke5er6ipm76rv7lnk0: A title and one row per total.
qpca9kmhultjkl2c07p9ch12gl: All the entries' cents added up.
vfe9ctmpbik6q99earj0gtdu2t: The entry with the fewest cents (the biggest expense, since spending is negative), or none for no entries.
901m48avisr5p7fgtujidu95un: The line about the smallest entry: its amount, date and memo.
680nlu9dkrfjt0g4jbvrrkaeug: Everything printed, in order: the two tables, the smallest entry, and the total with the count.
6g3v9kudoum4a87ndkkggn36dd: Prints the report, or stops if the file had no entries.
mvplvsvitbt9612ph2sn5tma13: Says how to run it, as an error, and gives exit code 2.
h0e4hvae9hf5m3okikk2uju81n: Reads the file, turns its lines into entries and shows the ledger; exit code 0.
ff3o42glsginuo7tvf8gjajeb6: Prints why it stopped, as an error, and gives exit code 1.
